title: Seafood Italian Squid Ink Gnocchi in Lobster Broth
summary: Immerse your palate in authentic Italian coastal flavors with this luxury seafood gnocchi recipe. Handcrafted squid ink potato dumplings are paired with tender lobster meat, sweet shrimp, and bay scallops in a rich tomato-seafood emulsion. This sophisticated dish represents high-end coastal dining from Venetia, where dramatic dark gnocchi contrast with bright red tomatoes and fresh green herbs. The tender seafood dumpling dough combines delicate riced potatoes with squid ink and semolina flour, creating a silky texture that absorbs flavorful broth seamlessly. Elevated with white wine, garlic, saffron, and extra virgin olive oil, every bite provides a oceanic burst balanced by subtle garden aromatics. Perfect for formal dinner parties or special celebrations, this recipe delivers an unforgettable Italian dining experience right in your home kitchen.

steps.step: Scrub russet potatoes under cold running water to clean skins thoroughly before boiling.
Place unpeeled potatoes into a large pot filled with cold salted water completely.
Bring water to a rolling boil over high heat and reduce to medium for steady simmering.
Cook potatoes for thirty minutes until a sharp knife pierces center without resistance.
Drain hot potatoes in a colander and allow steam to dissipate for five minutes carefully.
Peel warm potato skins using a paring knife while holding with a clean kitchen towel.
Pass warm peeled potatoes through a potato ricer directly onto a clean work surface.
Spread riced potatoes into an even thin layer to let steam escape and cool slightly.
Sprinkle one teaspoon of sea salt over cooling riced potatoes to season foundation evenly.
Dust onion powder and garlic powder across riced potatoes for initial aromatic seasoning.
Whisk egg yolk and squid ink together in a small dish until completely dark and uniform.
Pour squid ink egg mixture evenly over riced potatoes across the wooden board surface.
Sift all-purpose flour lightly over potatoes using a fine mesh sifter to avoid clumps.
Sprinkle semolina flour over flour layer to give dough optimal structural integrity.
Gently fold ingredients together using a bench scraper until dark dough starts to form.
Knead dough lightly for two minutes until squid ink color is evenly distributed throughout.
Form squid ink gnocchi dough into a smooth tender ball without overworking gluten strands.
Cut prepared black dough into eight equal portions using your bench scraper cleanly.
Dust wooden cutting board lightly with extra semolina flour to prevent sticking issue.
Roll one dough portion into a long rope approximately half an inch thick using palms.
Cut rope into uniform three-quarter inch dumpling pillows using a floured bench knife.
Roll each dumpling piece over a grooved wooden gnocchi board to form characteristic ridges.
Place shaped gnocchi onto a semolina-dusted parchment baking sheet in a single layer.
Repeat rolling and cutting steps for remaining seven portions of squid ink dough carefully.
Inspect shaped gnocchi to ensure ridges are deep enough to catch broth during plating.
Keep finished gnocchi covered loosely with a dry towel to avoid surface drying out.
Chill shaped gnocchi sheet in refrigerator for twenty minutes to firm texture before cooking.
Dust extra semolina over gnocchi if moisture causes slight sticking between pieces.
Verify all dumplings are of uniform size to ensure consistent cooking times in broth.
Prepare a large pot with two quarts water and coarse sea salt for dumpling boiling.
Set pot over high burner so water comes to a boil while broth sauce is prepared.
Clear workstation of loose flour to keep surrounding cooking area clean and organized.
Keep gnocchi cold until moment they are dropped into boiling water for optimal firm shape.
Reserve small dish of extra semolina for dusting hands during final cooking handling.
Pat raw shrimp dry with paper towels and cut each into bite-sized half-inch pieces.
Rinse bay scallops under cold water and pat dry thoroughly using clean paper towels.
Chop cooked lobster meat into clean bite-sized chunks on a separate plastic cutting board.
Season shrimp and scallops lightly with smoked paprika, black pepper, and salt in a bowl.
Heat one tablespoon of extra virgin olive oil in a wide sauté pan over medium-high heat.
Sear shrimp and scallops for ninety seconds until barely opaque, then remove immediately.
Transfer seared seafood to a clean plate, leaving flavorful juices inside hot skillet pan.
Add chopped lobster meat to seafood plate so all shellfish remains delicate and tender.
Cover seafood plate loosely with foil to retain warm temperatures and sweet juices.
Set aside seared seafood while building aromatic tomato and wine broth in same skillet.
Ensure seafood is not overcooked during initial sear as it finishes in hot broth later.
Inspect scallops to remove any remaining tough side muscle tags before cooking steps.
Drizzle half teaspoon lemon juice over seared shrimp to brighten coastal seafood flavors.
Keep seafood juices on plate reserved for stirring into broth sauce at final stage.
Maintain clean seafood prep area to prevent cross contamination during dinner assembly.
Check that all shellfish pieces are uniform size for even distribution across dishes.
Refrigerate raw elements promptly if timing between preparation steps extends longer.
Add remaining olive oil to skillet along with diced shallots over medium flame setting.
Sauté shallots for two minutes until translucent and soft before adding minced garlic.
Stir in minced garlic, fennel seeds, and red pepper flakes, cooking for one minute aromatically.
Add tomato paste and anchovy paste, stirring continuously until toasted and fragrant.
Pour in brandy and deglaze pan bottom, scraping up brown bits with wooden spoon carefully.
Add dry white wine and simmer rapidly for three minutes until liquid reduces by half.
Stir in seafood stock, clam juice, and saffron threads to infuse golden color and aroma.
Add crushed San Marzano tomatoes, dried oregano, and dried bay leaf to simmering broth base.
Reduce heat to low and simmer broth gently for fifteen minutes to marry rich flavors.
Add cherry tomato halves and capers to broth, simmering for three extra minutes softly.
Stir in heavy cream and unsalted butter to create a silky, rich seafood broth emulsion.
Season broth with lemon zest, black pepper, and extra sea salt according to taste preference.
Remove bay leaf from skillet and discard before combining gnocchi and seafood components.
Keep broth gently warm on low heat while boiling squid ink gnocchi in adjacent pot.
Check broth consistency to ensure it coats back of spoon without feeling overly heavy.
Taste broth for balanced acidity and add drop of lemon juice if richer depth needed.
Bring reserved pot of salted water to a rapid rolling boil over highest stove burner.
Carefully drop chilled squid ink gnocchi into boiling water in two separate batches.
Stir water gently with wooden spoon once to prevent dumplings from sticking to pot bottom.
Cook gnocchi for two to three minutes until all black dumplings float to water surface.
Allow floating gnocchi to simmer for thirty additional seconds to ensure center is cooked.
Use slotted spider spoon to transfer cooked gnocchi directly into warm broth skillet.
Repeat boiling process for second batch of gnocchi, transferring immediately when cooked.
Add seared shrimp, scallops, lobster meat, and reserved juices into warm broth skillet.
Toss gnocchi and seafood gently in broth for two minutes to warm components through.
Stir in chopped pitted kalamata olives to add dark briny balance to sweet seafood.
Fold in fresh basil and chopped flat-leaf parsley right at end of cooking process.
Verify dumpling coating is complete and broth is glossy and fragrant throughout skillet.
Remove pan from heat source immediately to prevent overcooking delicate seafood items.
Check temperature of dish to ensure all ingredients are steaming hot before plating.
Adjust seasoning with final pinch of sea salt and crack of black pepper if desired.
Prepare wide shallow pasta bowls near stove for immediate hot plating service.
Ladle rich saffron seafood broth evenly into four pre-warmed shallow stoneware bowls.
Divide black squid ink gnocchi dumplings equally among bowls, piling gently in center.
Arrange cooked lobster chunks, shrimp, and bay scallops artfully over gnocchi mounds.
Scatter cherry tomato halves and pitted olives around edges of each gnocchi bowl.
Drizzle white truffle oil lightly over each portion to elevate luxury aromatic profile.
Garnish top of dumplings with toasted pine nuts for subtle crunchy texture element.
Sprinkle chopped fresh chives and tarragon leaves over seafood for vibrant finish.
Top each bowl with grated pecorino romano cheese and delicate fresh microgreens nicely.
Wipe outer bowl rims clean with damp cloth to present immaculate chef-level display.
Serve immediately while seafood is tender and gnocchi dumplings remain hot and pillow-soft.
Pair with crisp Italian Pinot Grigio or Vermentino wine to complement seafood broth notes.
Provide warm crusty Italian bread on table for dipping into remaining saffron broth.
Instruct guests to mix black gnocchi with red broth for optimal flavor in every bite.
Refrigerate any remaining gnocchi and broth separately within airtight container promptly.
Reheat leftovers gently in covered pan over low heat with splash of additional stock.
Enjoy this sophisticated Italian culinary classic highlighting dark gnocchi and seafood.
